title: 13. Une entreprise, deux lois
gist: Multinational companies increasingly find themselves stuck between American and Chinese law: obeying one often means breaking the other. China is suing JPMorgan and Citigroup for following US sanctions rules, and forced Meta to unwind a $2bn AI deal (Manus). A new Chinese law taking effect in September will let China stop people from leaving the country. Firms are splitting off their China operations to limit the risk.

body.fr: Une grande entreprise américaine travaille aussi {{en Chine|in China}}.

bd.meaning: A big American company also works in China.
chunks: a big American company (grande before the noun)
bd.key: en + country = “in.” Use en before feminine countries like la Chine.

body.fr: Elle {{doit respecter|has to follow}} les lois américaines et les lois chinoises.

bd.meaning: It has to follow American laws and Chinese laws.
bd.key: devoir + plain verb = “has to.” Only doit changes; respecter stays plain.

body.fr: Mais parfois, les deux lois {{se contredisent|contradict each other}}.

bd.meaning: But sometimes, the two laws contradict each other.
bd.key: se + verb = a reflexive action. se contredire = “to contradict each other/itself.”

body.fr: {{Obéir|to obey}} à une loi, {{c'est|that means}} {{désobéir|disobey}} à l'autre.

bd.meaning: Obeying one law means disobeying the other.
bd.key: “X, c'est Y” = “X means Y.” c'est links two ideas together.

body.fr: Par exemple, deux grandes banques américaines, JPMorgan et Citigroup, {{ont un problème|have a problem}} en Chine.

bd.meaning: For example, two big American banks, JPMorgan and Citigroup, have a problem in China.

body.fr: Des tribunaux chinois {{poursuivent|are suing}} les deux banques.

bd.meaning: Chinese courts are suing both banks.
bd.key: French present covers English “is/are -ing.” No separate continuous form is needed: poursuivent = “sue” or “are suing.”

body.fr: Les banques {{ont seulement obéi|only obeyed}} au gouvernement américain.

bd.meaning: The banks only obeyed the American government.
bd.key: avoir + past participle = the past. ont obéi = “obeyed.”

body.fr: Elles {{suivent|follow}} les règles américaines contre certaines entreprises chinoises.

bd.meaning: They follow American rules against certain Chinese companies.
bd.key: Present tense covers ongoing habits: suivent = “follow / are following.”

body.fr: Un autre exemple : Meta {{a acheté|bought}} une petite entreprise d'IA, Manus, pour deux milliards de dollars.

bd.meaning: Another example: Meta bought a small AI company, Manus, for two billion dollars.
bd.key: avoir + past participle = the past. a acheté = “bought.”

body.fr: La Chine {{n'est pas d'accord|does not agree}}.

bd.key: ne … pas sandwich wraps around est. être d'accord is a fixed phrase for “to agree.”

body.fr: Meta {{a annulé|cancelled}} l'achat {{pour rester|to stay}} en bons termes avec la Chine.

bd.meaning: Meta cancelled the purchase to stay on good terms with China.
chunks: to stay / in order to stay
en bons termes avec la Chine
bd.key: pour + plain verb = “in order to.” rester stays plain after pour.

body.fr: En septembre, une nouvelle loi chinoise {{va entrer en vigueur|will take effect}}.

bd.meaning: In September, a new Chinese law will take effect.
bd.key: aller + plain verb = the near future. Only va changes; entrer stays plain.

body.fr: Elle {{va permettre|will allow}} à la Chine d'{{empêcher|prevent}} des gens de {{quitter|leave}} le pays.

bd.meaning: It will allow China to stop people from leaving the country.
bd.key: permettre à qqn de + verb = “allow someone to.” Little words (à/de) link the two verbs together.

body.fr: Beaucoup d'entreprises {{ont peur|are afraid}} de cette nouvelle loi.

bd.meaning: Many companies are afraid of this new law.
bd.key: avoir peur = “to be afraid.” French says “have fear,” not “be afraid.”

body.fr: Alors, les entreprises {{séparent|separate}} leurs activités en Chine du reste du monde.

bd.meaning: So, companies separate their China operations from the rest of the world.
chunks: from the rest of the world
bd.key: “leurs” = their. Just like ses is his/her, leurs doesn't show gender either.

body.fr: Elles gardent leurs {{données importantes|important data}} loin de la Chine.

bd.meaning: They keep their important data far from China.
bd.key: Adjectives echo the noun's gender/number: importantes agrees with feminine plural données.

body.fr: Pour le moment, {{personne ne sait|nobody knows}} comment {{résoudre|solve}} ce problème.

bd.meaning: For now, nobody knows how to solve this problem.
bd.key: “personne ne + verb” = “nobody ___.” personne acts like a negative word, paired with ne.

grammar.fr: Elle va permettre à la Chine
grammar.en: aller + plain verb = the near future. Only aller changes with the subject; the second verb stays plain.
avoir + past participle = the past (passé composé). a changes with the subject; the main verb takes its past form.
“personne ne” is a negative word-pair, like ne … pas but meaning “nobody” instead of “not.”

quiz.q: Pourquoi Meta a-t-il annulé l'achat de Manus ?
quiz.a: Parce que la Chine n'est pas d'accord. (Because China does not agree.)

flag: I compressed the legal detail a lot: the real story involves China's 2021 anti-sanctions law, a Singaporean shipping firm also caught up in a separate case, and the technical idea of “secondary sanctions” — I left all of that out to keep the story concrete. empêcher des gens de quitter le pays is a plain-language stand-in for the technical term “entry and exit bans”; a French legal article would more likely say interdiction de sortie du territoire.
